question.text: $\mathrm{BeF}_2,$ is soluble in water whereas fluorides of other alkaline earth metals are insoluble because of

options.text: greater hydration energy of $\mathrm{Be}^{2+}$ ion as compared to its lattice energy.

solution.text: $\mathrm{Be}^{2+}$ being small in size is heavily hydrated and heat of hydration exceeds the lattice energy. Hence $\mathrm{BeF}_{2}$ is soluble in water.
